failure_summary.description: Follow-up constraints triggered new searches instead of retrieving and filtering matching cached results.
Search or filter outputs were not consistently assigned and saved correctly, including duplicate calls and unsaved results.
A hotel search was called with missing mandatory dates and explicit None values.
A round trip was represented with arrival_date instead of a separate reverse-direction return search.
A request for a good restaurant was not followed by sorting results by rating.

patch.reasoning: The cache, result-saving, required-argument, and flight-leg behaviors are already specified in the skill, so repeating them would not patch a gap. The skill does not say how to operationalize qualitative quality requests such as “good” or “highly rated”; this addition maps those requests to a supported rating sort without inventing a threshold.

edits.content: - For an explicit user request for the best, good, or highly rated hotels or restaurants, do not invent a rating cutoff. Sort the applicable search or filtered results by the documented rating column (`rating_hotels` or `rating_restaurants`) in descending order, and assign and save the sorted output under a unique key. Do not add a quality ranking when the user has not requested one.
